themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints spiked to 6 THIS WEEK, up 1100% from a 0.5 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.16), suggesting a sudden and coordinated wave of unauthorized signage, graffiti, or advertising across the district.
evidence: 6 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average (8-week baseline)
This is the most recent spike in the dataset, appearing in the current reporting week
reporting_angles: Ground-truth verification: visit specific blocks with complaints to document what type of illegal posting is occurring (gang tags, political ads, commercial posters)
Interview Parks Dept or Sanitation about enforcement response; ask if there's a known perpetrator or organized campaign

themes_detail.label: Dead Animals & Sanitation Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints hit 6 LAST WEEK, a 700% spike from 0.8 weekly average (z-score: 7.94), paired with 671 unsanitary condition complaints over 90 days, signaling potential public health hazard and environmental management breakdown.
evidence: 6 dead animal complaints last week vs. 0.8 weekly average (z-score: 7.94, high severity)
700% increase indicates anomaly, not normal variation
671 unsanitary condition complaints over 90-day period suggest broader sanitation infrastructure stress
Community Board has long-standing request for 'public health issues' interventions, still unfunded
reporting_angles: Interview DSNY about removal capacity and disease vectors; ask if decomposition is linked to pest infestation or waterborne issues
Contact NYC Health Dept about any disease surveillance alerts in Parkchester/Soundview in the past 2 weeks
Identify specific streets with multiple complaints; photograph and map the concentration

themes_detail.label: Derelict Vehicle Flood
themes_detail.summary: Derelict vehicle complaints jumped to 35 LAST WEEK, a 242% spike from 10.2 weekly average (z-score: 3.87), suggesting a sudden influx of abandoned or non-functional vehicles clogging streets and parking.
evidence: 35 complaints last week vs. 10.2 weekly average (z-score: 3.87)
Follows pattern of illegal parking (2035 complaints over 90 days) and blocked driveways (1165 complaints), suggesting parking crisis is accelerating
reporting_angles: Request NYPD/Sanitation data on tow rates this week; compare removal speed to complaint volume
Map hotspot streets where derelict vehicles are clustering; interview residents on impact to street access
Ask NYPD if there's a theft or chop-shop ring operating in the district

themes_detail.label: Lead Contamination Alert
themes_detail.summary: Lead complaints spiked to 9 THREE WEEKS AGO, a 350% increase from 2.0 weekly average (z-score: 5.72), potentially indicating discovery of lead paint, pipes, or soil contamination in older residential stock—critical for child health.
evidence: 9 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 2.0 weekly average (z-score: 5.72, high severity)
350% spike; Community Board has standing request to 'address illegal conversions and uses of buildings,' suggesting older, poorly maintained stock
Parkchester/Soundview has significant pre-1978 housing stock vulnerable to lead hazards
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Health Dept: were any children tested for elevated blood lead in Parkchester in the past month? Request any advisory notices issued.
Interview HPD about lead inspection enforcement and remediation timelines; ask which buildings generated complaints
Talk to parents and advocates about awareness of lead testing programs; identify gaps in outreach

themes_detail.label: Lot Condition & Environmental Blight
themes_detail.summary: Lot condition complaints jumped to 3 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 2300% anomaly from 0.1 weekly average (z-score: 8.69, highest z-score in dataset), indicating rapid deterioration of vacant or underdeveloped properties, compounded by missing street signs (4 complaints 3 weeks ago, 967% spike).
evidence: 3 lot condition complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average (z-score: 8.69, highest statistical severity in dataset)
Missing street signs spike (4 complaints 3 weeks ago, 967% increase, z-score: 7.49) suggests neighborhood wayfinding and maintenance collapse
Active ULURP rezoning at 1160 Pugsley Avenue (in public review) suggests property pressure and potential blight linked to development pipeline
reporting_angles: Identify which lots generated complaints; cross-reference with ULURP applications and tax delinquency records to determine if blight is speculative or deferred maintenance
Interview Sanitation and Parks Dept on lot maintenance authority and enforcement; ask why street signs are disappearing
Talk to Community Board about whether lot blight is concentrated near rezoning sites or dispersed; assess if environmental injustice theme exists
